decisions.reason: As a prominently launched next-generation core printer in a growing and R&D-intensive firm, it likely meets or is close enough to aspiration levels that management would continue backing it.

This software module extends the established coding offer and supports variable-data printing, so with organizational slack and strategic fit the firm would likely retain it unless performance clearly disappointed.
An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces fits the firm's core applications and customer needs closely, making continued market presence more likely than resource redeployment.
The decoding app is more peripheral and its results are more uncertain, but as a successor product aligned with digitalization and traceability the firm would probably keep it for now.
Inline code verification matches the firm's move toward end-to-end traceability, so even with uncertain early evidence a growing large firm would likely continue it.
Print layout design software complements the installed base and supports one-stop solutions, so management would likely judge it worth keeping while its market performance becomes clearer.
